Buddhaghoṣa
5th Cent.; born in a village near Buddhagaya; mastered the Vedas an. other branches of knowledge; was defeated by Revata, a Buddhist monk; while dwelling with Revata, he is said to have written Nāṇodaya (in Pāli) (See Cullavagga xxxvii. 225) an. the Atthasālinī an. began to write Parittaṭṭhakathā, a concise C. on the Tripiṭakas. He is said to have visited Ceylon, studied Sinihalese commentaries on the Tripiṭakas a. the Mahāvihāra under [Page020-a. Saṅghapāla. Some do not subscribe to this view. See Louis Finot, La legende de Buddhaghoṣa, Paris, 1921, p.. 101-19. He then wrote the C. s on the Tripiṭakas. See Dict. of Pāli Proper names II. p.. 306-7; Wint., HIL. II. p.. 192ff; B. C. Law, His. of Pāli Lit. II. p.. 388-9, 399-481 an. Life an. work of Buddhaghoṣa, Cal. Ori. Ser. 9.
His commentaries on the different sections of the Tripiṭaka texts are called differently.
